text:
alyssa-se: Customer kickoff: they need offline attestation + roll-forward/rollback policy for an air-gapped POC. Key asks: can we sign patches using customer HSM, and what's the cadence we recommend to avoid too many forced upgrades?

jen-pm: TL;DR: yes we can integrate with customer-managed HSM for signing at their side, and we can offer a staggered cadence (weekly patch window or monthly major) depending on risk appetite. Need eng/security for details.

noah-eng: implementation notes: we support bundle signing via customer HSM or our signing service. For airgap transfers we support chunked patch files (we call them "patch shards") with manifest+hash. Verifier runs on node at install time.

noah-eng: we also have a lightweight attestation artifact (JSON + compact signature) that includes artifact_hash, manifest_version, build_tag, and signer_fingerprint. verifier rejects if not in allowed set.

tori-sec: threat considerations: if customer uses their HSM keys we treat them as authoritative for origin. That shifts liability—legal needs to sign off. For key compromise: we need a revocation distribution mechanism (signed CRL or short-lived delegations). Also, retention of attestation logs for audits is a separate charge.

omar-sales: pricing: customer asked if HSM integration, signed CRL distribution, and emergency on-call are separate line items. What should I quote?

noah-eng: scoping inputs from sales: 1) expected number of hosts to validate per POC, 2) expected patch shard frequency, 3) acceptable patch window length (min downtime), 4) whether they want us to host an in-VPC notary for signed proofs or prefer on-prem-only.

jen-pm: added: also whether they want signed deltas only (smaller transfers) or full-image replacements. Deltas reduce transfer size but complicate rollbacks if multiple deltas chain.

tori-sec: operational requirement: emergency rollback must be pre-approved and auditable. Two secure options: pre-signed rollback tokens (customer creates via HSM) OR a delegated emergency signer (we keep an emergency key pair inside our escrow, activated only with multi-party auth). Each has tradeoffs.

omar-sales: customer prefers pre-signed tokens in their KMS. They want a documented runbook and an SLA for us to help if token rotation causes failing installs. Can we commit to a 4-hour emergency assist?

legalbot: SLA note: 4-hour emergency assist is possible for enterprise contracts with on-call premium. We need to add an indemnity carve-out: if customer-managed keys are compromised, vendor liability limited. Also include change control clause for emergency activations.

alyssa-se: can eng draft a simple runbook snippet for pre-signed token flow and a fallback flow? customer wants the one-pager in the SOW by COB Wed.

noah-eng: runbook draft below:
```
PRE-SIGNED TOKEN ROLLBACK (draft):
- Preconditions: customer generates rollback_token using their HSM; token stored in customer vault and uploaded to SOW artifact bucket (hash only).
- Step 1: RDC verifies token hash against SOW manifest.
- Step 2: Customer transfers patch_shard via approved transport.
- Step 3: On target node, operator runs `rdx apply --rollback --token <token>`; verifier checks token signature and manifest hash.
- Step 4: Run smoke tests, collect logs, push attestation record to audit bucket.
- Step 5: If token misuse detected, rotate HSM key and publish revocation to nodes at next maintenance window.
```

omar-sales: nice. i'll bundle that with pricing tiers: Basic (tooling + docs), Plus (one-time HSM integration + quarterly validation), Premium (24/7 emergency assist + retention for audit logs).

jen-pm: ops: what about upgrade cadence guidance? customer worried about frequent micro-patches causing operational churn in an air-gapped site.

noah-eng: recommendation: micro-patches (security patches) every 2 weeks max; functional changes monthly. We can buffer micro-patches into a single monthly minibatch for air-gapped installs to minimize transfers. That can be an opt-in config for their private deploy.

tori-sec: note: batching patches into monthly minibatches increases blast radius. Customer must accept tradeoff between transfer overhead and time-to-fix. Document risk in SOW decision matrix.

legalbot: security questionnaire flag: "Customer-managed key indemnity"; require explicit acceptance and a support escrow process if customer requests vendor to sign on their behalf in emergencies.

alyssa-se: action items: @noah-eng produce the runbook + sample CLI commands, @tori-sec produce short threat checklist and CRL distribution options, @omar-sales draft pricing tiers and SOW language for indemnity/escrow, @jen-pm assemble one-pager. Deadline: COB Wed.

deploy-bot: Ticket created INF-7710 "airgap HSM attestation + rollback SOW" assigned to noah-eng and tori-sec.

omar-sales: following up tomorrow with the customer to confirm host counts and whether they'll opt into monthly minibatches. :slightly_smiling_face: 

jen-pm: thanks team — ping me if legal needs clarifications.

alyssa-se: closing loop here, leaving single-thread summary for the customer doc.
